title: Carl "Bama" Warwick and the 1974 jazz cruise
summary: Callender recalls his schoolmate Carl Warwick, who played in white and Black bands and invited him to a party for Ella Fitzgerald on the cruise.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: You mentioned a few minutes ago off the tape that you picked up a book off the bookshelf here, and ran into a name.

Yes. The first name I saw was Carl Warwick, who they called Bama. Well, we were in the same band in school. I mean, we went to school... I think we were even in the same class. Well, in later years, Carl played with mostly White bands, although he never did claim to be White. He was like another Willie Smith. He could have been anything. But I guess his background was from mostly Caucasian. But he never did claim to be anything but just another person.
He was a good friend of Dizzy's, I know. Because I heard Dizzy talk about him.

Oh yeah, they were very good friends. As a matter of fact, he was one of the sponsors of the first Jazz cruise, the one that I was on that I went on... I didn't play; I just went to be a spectator. And I saw him. As a matter of fact, he was the one who invited us up to the Captain's cabin for a party for Ella Fitzgerald, and knowing him made me fortunate enough to get invited to the party --
because he was one of the sponsors. So that's Carl "Bama." I think Carl played with Woody Herman and a lot of White bands, and also a lot of Black bands. He could have been anything he wanted to be.
And that Jazz cruise was when?
In 1974, just after Duke Ellington passed.
That's the one you were on your way to when you heard the news.
Yeah, we were on our way to that when we heard of Duke's passing.
